title: Later attention queries rescued selected early-loop retrieval errors
summary: Moving same-item later-loop attention queries into the first loop corrected 89.8% and 96.9% of selected synthetic two-hop errors in two Ouro models. Queries shuffled between items corrected 23.7% and 20.6%, respectively. The result applies to questions answered incorrectly in the first loop and correctly later.

source_review.scope: v1 query swap Methods, Table 2 and natural-question caveats

evidence.tested: The primary synthetic test included 600 scenes per model, with 245 and 223 qualifying early-loop errors, respectively. Same-item and shuffled queries were compared at aligned positions.
evidence.unknown: Natural-question rescue was smaller and did not establish bridge redirection. A positional contribution remains possible. In Ouro-1.4B the rescue changes four-candidate ranking, not greedy generated answers. The intervention supplies a separate query at every layer/head, not one vector; the two model sizes share developmental history.
evidence.ai_role: The authors intervened on pretrained Ouro attention query activations and compared matched late-loop and shuffled donors.
